rows.definition: The OpenAI Responses-wire cross-shard cache-routing hint (prompt_cache_key): a stable key derived from the cacheable HEAD that pins requests sharing a prefix onto one upstream automatic-prefix-cache node (#5186).
rows.distinction: A routing/affinity hint on the auto prefix cache (miss only costs latency), distinct from the Anthropic managed-cache TTL upgrade (c4681-cachettlupgrade) which extends explicit cache_control breakpoint lifetime.

rows.definition: loop_constraint.go is the agent package's loop-side consumer of the out-of-band add-constraint op (#2756): applyConstraints drains the sessionctl constraint mailbox at the turn boundary and carries the tightened floor's standing directive as a system notice, and constraintDenied denies a floor-forbidden tool call before dispatch with a typed receipt carrying the closed CONSTRAINT_* reason.
rows.distinction: Not loop_redirect.go (which folds an operator redirect into the live OBJECTIVE - what the session pursues): loop_constraint.go folds operator constraints into the live FLOOR - what the session MAY DO - and enforces it per tool call; and not the trajctl metaloop, which walks intents, not turns.

rows.definition: loop_park.go is the agent package's loop-side consumer of the out-of-band operator approve/deny inbox (#2757): parkEscalatedDeny intercepts an ESCALATE-gated deny at the dispatch site when the session's inbox is open, parks it on the sessionctl pending-action queue, and honors the external verdict — approve re-proposes the call through the normal syscall boundary (byte-identical plus the gate's confirm echo, or operator-modified args freshly adjudicated), deny/timeout abort with a typed receipt carrying the closed PARK_* reason.
rows.distinction: Not loop_constraint.go (which folds operator constraints into the live FLOOR before dispatch): loop_park.go resolves a call the gate ALREADY refused with an ESCALATE disposition, parking it for an EXTERNAL operator verdict instead of returning the deny straight to the model; and not the trajctl metaloop, which walks intents, not turns.

rows.definition: loop_observe.go is the agent package's OUTBOUND loop-state seam (#5148): WithProgressObserver installs a typed, nil-safe ProgressObserver that runArm emits closed-set ProgressEvent lifecycle transitions through (turn_started, tool_started, call_adjudicated, result_admitted, turn_done), which the native gateway stream renders as structured SSE. Unset, every emit is a no-op and the loop is byte-for-byte the historical loop.
rows.distinction: Not loop_constraint.go / loop_park.go, which are INBOUND seams that drain operator ops at the turn boundary and CHANGE what the loop does (the floor it enforces, the park it takes): loop_observe.go is purely OUTBOUND and read-only — it publishes witnessed transitions the loop already made and can never gate, deny, or alter a turn.

rows.definition: call_adjudicated (Go const ProgressCallAdjudicated) is the loop-progress event KIND that publishes one tool call's already-decided kernel verdict on the native owned-loop SSE stream (#5148): it carries Turn, CallID, Tool, Verdict (ALLOW/DENY/TRANSFORM/QUARANTINE) and, on a deny, the closed refusal reason a client gates on.
rows.distinction: Not 'adjudicating' (the decision act itself, performed by the kernel's adjudicator rungs): call_adjudicated is the after-the-fact OBSERVATION of that act, emitted on the stream once the verdict is final. It decides nothing and can change no verdict; suppressing it would leave the adjudication outcome identical.

rows.definition: loop_midflight.go is the agent package's owned per-run MID-FLIGHT verb mailbox and tamper-evident hash-chained journal (#5158, the write half of #2403 / epic #2388): a transport enqueues interrupt / drop-pending-call / set-budget verbs that the owned loop consumes at its next CLEAN turn boundary (never mid-tool, never mid-adjudication) to stop the arm, skip one named queued call, or write a fresh budget through to the session table; nil-safe, so with no verb issued the loop is byte-for-byte the historical loop.
rows.distinction: Not loop_observe.go, the OUTBOUND read-only half of the same owned-turn program that only PUBLISHES witnessed lifecycle transitions and can alter no turn: loop_midflight is INBOUND and MUTATING, stopping or steering the live arm at the boundary and sealing at return. And not loop_constraint.go / loop_park.go, which drain sessionctl OPERATOR ops (floor tightening / escalated-deny parking): loop_midflight is the per-run SESSION-verb mailbox (interrupt/drop/set-budget) whose journal is hash-chained tamper-evidence.

rows.definition: Config predicate reporting whether a *KVCache is a COMPLETE session prefix for this architecture — i.e. whether cloning the cache carries the whole of what the session already ingested. True for cached architectures whose per-layer K/V rows are the entire state; false for the gemma4 recompute bridge, whose state is the token history and whose cache stays empty.
rows.distinction: ExactSpanSupported asks whether an engine can EVICT an exact span from a cache it already holds; this asks whether the cache IS the state at all. A recompute architecture answers yes to neither, but for different reasons: eviction is inert because there are no rows, while prefix reuse is unsound because the rows were never where the prefix lived.

rows.definition: Reports whether the normal request-owned prefix acquisition route can perform deadline admission using usable cached-prefix credit; speculative routes remain cold-admitted.
rows.distinction: KVPrefixReuseSupported concerns whether a KV cache contains complete reusable session state; this predicate concerns whether this planner route has the owned-prefix execution boundary required to grant deadline credit.

rows.definition: Owns the planner-owned single native forward slot shared by ordinary requests and decode cohorts, supporting cancellation-aware waiters without detached lock-acquisition goroutines.
rows.distinction: ExecutionDeadlineAdmissionSupported identifies deadline-credit capability at a prefix boundary; this gate controls exclusive concurrent access to the device forward slot and does not estimate deadline feasibility.

rows.definition: Concrete adapter to result-bearing Model.StepV41Batch with untouched unselected scalar fallback and owner-busy wait.
rows.distinction: Executes prepared-lane decoding rather than reporting coordinator cleanup; does not activate serving.

rows.definition: Private driver aggregate of completed shared-head panels and rows returned by model operations.
rows.distinction: Completed-operation counts rather than the concrete decode adapter; no physical throughput claim.

rows.definition: Private callbacks for batch attempt, acquiring scalar fallback and cancellation-aware busy wait.
rows.distinction: Operation bundle rather than completed-operation receipt or capability declaration.

rows.definition: Stable-ID decode state machine retaining sampled token, emission and penalty/RNG state across busy retries and scattering outcomes without selected replay.
rows.distinction: Execution algorithm rather than callback bundle.

rows.definition: One stable lane slot retains Session identity, chosen token and pending-forward state across retries and compaction.
rows.distinction: Uncommitted request progress rather than completed-operation aggregate.

rows.definition: Selects a decode lane request context, falling back to driver context.
rows.distinction: Cancellation authority selection rather than retained token progress; creates no context and does not cancel healthy peers.

rows.definition: Post-operation check of unique exact lane-ID coverage and untouched unselected results before fallback.
rows.distinction: No-replay protocol validation rather than executing concrete model wiring.

rows.definition: Applies one validated stable-ID outcome, updating history only on commit and preserving committed errors and actual forward kind.
rows.distinction: Commit-aware mutation rather than pre-scatter validation.

rows.definition: Decode-algorithm discriminator and Qwen/V41 values separating unlike queued requests into contiguous FIFO cohorts.
rows.distinction: Queue grouping and Flash lane bounds rather than pending token progress or backend capability.

rows.definition: Associates a request with its prepared decode lane and unknown panic published by closure completion.
rows.distinction: Prepared-request lifecycle rather than pending sampled-token state; creates no Session lock.

rows.definition: Terminal no-replay outcome for unfinished or unstarted requests in an aborted selected Flash cohort.
rows.distinction: Selected-cohort termination rather than retained request state or untouched fallback eligibility.

rows.definition: Existing Qwen algorithm selector for contiguous queue grouping.
rows.distinction: Selects Qwen execution rather than the Flash four-lane grouping variant.

rows.definition: Flash algorithm selector for bounded four-lane contiguous FIFO cohorts.
rows.distinction: Selects the Flash member of the decode-kind discriminator, distinct from Qwen; neither grouping value declares backend capability.

rows.definition: Selects each decode lane request cancellation/deadline context with driver-context fallback.
rows.distinction: Context-family view of the same helper: cancellation authority rather than gateway decode flow or retained token progress; creates no new context.

rows.definition: Associates a Qwen coalesced request with its prepared decode lane and an unknown panic captured by its completion closure.
rows.distinction: Qwen request/lane/unknown-panic association rather than V4.1 per-request participation and row accounting, retained sampled-token progress awaiting a forward, or a terminal cohort-abort outcome; it creates no Session lock.

rows.definition: Terminal no-replay sentinel for affected peer or unstarted work in an aborted selected Qwen cohort; the originating unknown panic is retained separately for cleanup-ordered propagation.
rows.distinction: The selected Qwen cohort's terminal no-replay marker, not retained request/lane state, the V4.1-specific abort marker, or permission to retry through scalar fallback.
